course.title: Modern Frontend Web Development with React — Initial cohort draft
course.shortDescription: Six guided classes covering web foundations and modern javascript; components, state and effects; routing and application structure; forms and accessible interactions; server data and responsive dashboards; testing, performance and delivery.
course.description:
A guided course for learners who want to build and explain a working student-management application.

Outcomes

  1. Build a semantic catalogue with five courses, a heading, navigation, and labelled level filter. Explain why filtering should preserve the original array. Test an empty result and restore all courses.
  2. Create three reusable course cards and a parent selection summary. Add a counter whose document title follows its state. Explain which data is a prop, local state, derived value, or external synchronization.
  3. Implement Home, Courses, About and Profile pages plus a course detail route. Test a bookmarked detail URL, an invalid ID, an unknown route and browser Back. Document the host fallback required for a direct visit.
  4. Build the student registration form with name, email, phone and course. Show field-specific errors, a pending state and a retry path that preserves values. Test it with only a keyboard and a deliberately rejected request.
  5. Connect a course API to a responsive dashboard. Demonstrate loading, empty, error and success states. Test long course titles at 360 px and explain which query should refresh after enrollment changes.
  6. Deliver the catalogue as a local production preview. Include one behavior test, a bundle size observation, direct-route evidence and a deployment runbook. Explain a measured optimization and a rollback procedure.
course.duration: 6 classes · 18 live hours plus independent practice
course.requirements: Basic computer use, a code editor, a browser and a local development environment. Frontend framework tracks assume basic JavaScript; backend tracks include introductory language review.
course.targetAudience: Learners building their first structured web application; instructors should review prerequisites with the cohort.

class.title: 01. Web foundations and modern JavaScript
class.objectives: Explain web foundations and modern javascript; implement the demonstrated workflow; test a normal and a failure case; justify design choices using evidence.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: Build a course catalogue from data before adding a framework. HTML supplies document meaning, CSS controls presentation, and JavaScript transforms data and responds to actions. An API is the boundary between the browser and protected backend operations.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Start with an array of course objects with stable IDs. Use filter to select records and map to transform each result. Both return new arrays; neither requires changing the source array. A const binding cannot be reassigned, but its object can still be mutated. Prefer copying when preparing UI data. A promise describes a future result: await it inside an async function and handle rejection explicitly. Keep credentials and authorization decisions on the server.

sections.title: Worked demonstration
sections.body:
Read the example, predict its output or behavior, then run it in the appropriate project. Framework snippets assume the lesson project and the shown imports or surrounding setup. Inspect the result before making the extension below.

const courses = [{id: 1, title: 'React', level: 'Beginner'}, {id: 2, title: 'APIs', level: 'Intermediate'}];
const titles = courses.filter(c => c.level === 'Beginner').map(c => c.title);
console.log(titles); // ['React']

sections.title: Guided practical exercise
sections.body:
Build a semantic catalogue with five courses, a heading, navigation, and labelled level filter. Explain why filtering should preserve the original array. Test an empty result and restore all courses.

Work in a disposable project using synthetic student data. Record expected behavior before running it. Compare the result with your prediction and explain one mistake you corrected.

questions.text: What is the primary responsibility of a frontend application?

options.text: Providing the user interface and client-side functionality

questions.explanation: The frontend is responsible for the interface users interact with and client-side application behavior.

questions.text: Which technology is primarily responsible for defining the structure of a web page?
questions.explanation: HTML defines the structure and semantic content of web pages.

questions.text: What is CSS primarily used for?
questions.explanation: CSS controls presentation, including colors, spacing, typography, positioning, and responsive layouts.

questions.text: Which technology is primarily responsible for adding programming logic to a web application in the browser?
questions.explanation: JavaScript provides programming logic and enables interactive behavior in web applications.

questions.text: What is an API commonly used for in a frontend application?

options.text: Connecting the frontend to backend services

questions.explanation: APIs allow frontend applications to communicate with backend services and exchange data.

questions.text: A React application needs to display a list of products retrieved from a backend. What does the frontend typically need to do?

options.text: Request the products through an API and render the response
Restart the server for every request

questions.explanation: A frontend normally communicates with the backend through an API rather than directly accessing the database.

questions.text: Which keyword declares a variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: `const` prevents reassignment of the variable binding.

questions.text: What does an arrow function provide in modern JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Arrow functions provide a concise syntax for defining functions.

questions.text: Which array method creates a new array by transforming each element?
questions.explanation: `map()` applies a function to each element and returns a new array containing the results.

questions.text: What does `filter()` generally do?

options.text: Returns elements that satisfy a condition

questions.explanation: `filter()` creates a new array containing elements that pass a specified condition.

class.title: 02. Components, state and effects
class.objectives: Explain components, state and effects; implement the demonstrated workflow; test a normal and a failure case; justify design choices using evidence.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: A component describes a reusable part of an interface. A parent passes props; state belongs to the component that owns an interaction. Rendering calculates the UI from these inputs.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Extract CourseCard when several cards share structure. Keep a selected course ID in the nearest common parent when a list and detail panel both need it. Use functional state updates when the next value depends on the previous value. Effects synchronize with external systems such as document titles or subscriptions; derived values can usually be calculated during rendering. Include every reactive dependency, and return cleanup for subscriptions so mounting and unmounting do not leave duplicate listeners.

sections.title: Worked demonstration
sections.body:
Read the example, predict its output or behavior, then run it in the appropriate project. Framework snippets assume the lesson project and the shown imports or surrounding setup. Inspect the result before making the extension below.

function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; }, [count]);
  return <button onClick={() => setCount(n => n + 1)}>{count}</button>;
}

questions.text: What is a React component?

options.text: A reusable piece of UI and application logic

questions.explanation: Components are reusable building blocks used to construct React interfaces.

questions.text: What are props in React?

options.text: Data passed from a component to another component

questions.explanation: Props allow data and configuration to be passed into components.

questions.text: Which React Hook is commonly used to manage component state?
questions.explanation: `useState` allows functional components to maintain state.

questions.text: What usually happens when React state changes?

options.text: The component may re-render with the updated state

questions.explanation: A state update causes React to schedule a re-render so the UI can reflect the new state.

questions.text: Why are reusable components valuable in React?

options.text: They eliminate the need for JavaScript
They reduce duplication and improve maintainability

questions.explanation: Reusable components allow common UI and behavior to be implemented once and reused throughout an application.

questions.text: A parent component needs to provide a student's name to a child component. What is the standard React approach?

options.text: Pass the name as a prop

questions.explanation: Props are the standard mechanism for passing data from parent components to child components.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of `useEffect`?

options.text: Perform side effects in a component

questions.explanation: `useEffect` is commonly used for side effects such as API requests, subscriptions, and interacting with external systems.

questions.text: When does an effect with an empty dependency array `[]` generally run after the component mounts?

options.text: It generally runs after the initial render
It runs only when the server restarts

questions.explanation: An effect with an empty dependency array generally runs after the component's initial render, with development-mode behavior potentially causing an additional invocation under Strict Mode.

questions.text: What is `useMemo` primarily intended to help with?
questions.explanation: `useMemo` can cache an expensive calculation until its dependencies change.

questions.text: What is `useCallback` primarily used for?
questions.explanation: `useCallback` memoizes a function reference and can help avoid unnecessary renders in certain component structures.

class.title: 03. Routing and application structure
class.objectives: Explain routing and application structure; implement the demonstrated workflow; test a normal and a failure case; justify design choices using evidence.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: A route gives a screen an address that can be bookmarked and opened directly. A useful application handles direct entry, nested pages, and missing resources as carefully as navigation clicks.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Separate the shared layout from page components. Use a route parameter for the course ID and validate it before requesting data. A missing route and a known route with a missing course need appropriate not-found states. Query parameters suit shareable filters. A client-side protected route improves navigation but does not authorize API requests: the server must verify the account and enrollment. In production, configure the host to serve the application entry point for valid client routes.

sections.title: Worked demonstration
sections.body:
Read the example, predict its output or behavior, then run it in the appropriate project. Framework snippets assume the lesson project and the shown imports or surrounding setup. Inspect the result before making the extension below.

// Route pattern: /courses/:courseId
const { courseId } = useParams();
const id = Number(courseId);
if (!Number.isInteger(id) || id <= 0) return <p>Course not found</p>;
return <CourseDetails id={id} />;

questions.text: What is client-side routing used for in a React application?

options.text: Navigating between application views without requiring a full page reload

questions.explanation: Client-side routing allows single-page applications to display different views based on the URL.

questions.text: Which library is commonly used for routing in React applications?
questions.explanation: React Router is a widely used routing library for React applications.

questions.text: A route is `/students/:id`. What does `:id` typically represent?
questions.explanation: Dynamic route parameters allow a URL segment to represent a variable value such as a student's ID.

questions.text: Why should a large React application be divided into logical components and modules?

options.text: To remove the need for browsers

questions.explanation: Good application structure makes large applications easier to understand, test, maintain, and extend.

questions.text: A user visits `/courses/15`. The application needs to retrieve course 15. What is a suitable approach?

options.text: Query the database directly from the browser
Read the route parameter and use it when requesting course data

questions.explanation: The route parameter can be extracted and used to request the corresponding resource from the backend API.

questions.text: What is a protected route?

options.text: A route that requires certain conditions such as authentication before access
A route that only contains CSS
A route that cannot contain JavaScript

questions.explanation: Protected routes restrict access to users who satisfy requirements such as being authenticated or having a particular role.

questions.text: A bookmarked course URL works through a link but returns 404 on refresh. What should you check?

options.text: The host fallback for client-side routes

questions.explanation: The server must serve the application entry point for valid client-side URLs.

questions.text: Where should an API enforce enrollment access?

options.text: Only in a React route guard

questions.explanation: Client navigation checks cannot prevent direct API calls.

questions.text: Which value belongs in a shareable course-filter URL?
questions.explanation: A query parameter can preserve a non-secret filter for direct visits.

questions.text: A valid detail route contains an unknown course ID. What should the page show?
questions.explanation: A valid route can still identify a missing resource.

class.title: 04. Forms and accessible interactions
class.objectives: Explain forms and accessible interactions; implement the demonstrated workflow; test a normal and a failure case; justify design choices using evidence.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: A registration form coordinates user input, validation and a request to the server. Treat submitting, success and failure as distinct states so a slow request does not appear to lose the response.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Controlled inputs read their displayed value from state and update that state on change. Associate each label with its field and connect error text with aria-describedby. Validate required fields before sending, but also enforce the same business rules on the server because browser checks can be bypassed. Preserve values on failure, prevent duplicate submissions while pending, and move attention to actionable errors. A placeholder is an example, not a replacement for a label.

sections.title: Worked demonstration
sections.body:
Read the example, predict its output or behavior, then run it in the appropriate project. Framework snippets assume the lesson project and the shown imports or surrounding setup. Inspect the result before making the extension below.

const [email, setEmail] = useState('');
<label htmlFor="email">Email</label>
<input id="email" type="email" required value={email}
  onChange={e => setEmail(e.target.value)} />

questions.text: What is a controlled input in React?

options.text: An input controlled only by CSS
An input whose value is managed through React state
An input controlled by the database
An input that cannot receive text

questions.explanation: Controlled inputs use React state as the source of truth for their current value.

questions.text: Why is client-side form validation useful?

options.text: It provides immediate feedback to users
It removes the need for APIs

questions.explanation: Client-side validation improves user experience by identifying obvious errors before submission.

questions.text: Why should backend validation still be performed even when frontend validation exists?
questions.explanation: Client-side validation can be bypassed, so the backend must independently validate incoming data.

questions.text: A login form contains email and password fields. What should happen after a successful submission?

options.text: The application should process the authentication response and update the user's authenticated state
The application should delete the form

questions.explanation: A successful login typically results in authentication state being established and the UI being updated accordingly.

questions.text: What is a common way to prevent a form from performing the browser's default submission behavior in React?
questions.explanation: `event.preventDefault()` prevents the browser's default action, allowing React to handle the submission.

questions.text: A registration form submits invalid data returned by the backend. What is a good frontend behavior?

options.text: Display the relevant validation errors to the user

questions.explanation: Backend validation errors should be mapped into useful feedback so the user can correct the form.

questions.text: A registration request fails. What is the most useful form behavior?

options.text: Preserve entered values and show an actionable error

questions.explanation: Retaining input lets the student correct or retry the request.

questions.text: What connects a visible form label to its input?
questions.explanation: The programmatic association helps both clicking and assistive technology.

questions.text: Why must the server validate a form that React already validated?

options.text: A caller can bypass browser validation

questions.explanation: Only server validation covers all clients and direct requests.

questions.text: When should a submit button prevent duplicate requests?

options.text: While the current submission is pending
Only when the browser is offline

questions.explanation: A pending state prevents accidental duplicate sends while preserving later retries.

class.title: 05. Server data and responsive dashboards
class.objectives: Explain server data and responsive dashboards; implement the demonstrated workflow; test a normal and a failure case; justify design choices using evidence.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: Remote data has a lifecycle beyond component state: it can be loading, stale, refreshed or unavailable. A dashboard should remain understandable in each state and at narrow viewport widths.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Choose a query key containing all inputs that identify the request, such as course and cohort IDs. After a mutation, invalidate affected data rather than manually assuming the server result. Distinguish an empty array from a failed request. Keep filters and open panels as local UI state. Build layout with flexible columns, allow long text to wrap, and preserve visible focus. Measure responsiveness with realistic content and loading states, not only a short successful response.

sections.title: Worked demonstration
sections.body:
Read the example, predict its output or behavior, then run it in the appropriate project. Framework snippets assume the lesson project and the shown imports or surrounding setup. Inspect the result before making the extension below.

const query = useQuery({queryKey: ['courses', level], queryFn: () => fetchCourses(level)});
if (query.isPending) return <p role="status">Loading courses...</p>;
if (query.isError) return <button onClick={() => query.refetch()}>Retry</button>;
return <CourseList courses={query.data} />;

questions.text: What is application state?

options.text: Data that can change during the application's lifetime

questions.explanation: State represents data whose current value affects application behavior or what is displayed.

questions.text: Which tool is commonly suitable for simple local component state?
questions.explanation: `useState` is appropriate for managing state that belongs primarily to an individual component.

questions.text: What is server state?

options.text: Data contained in the browser's HTML parser
Data managed by a backend or remote server

questions.explanation: Server state includes remotely managed data such as users, courses, orders, and API responses.

questions.text: Why might a library such as TanStack Query be useful in a React application?

options.text: It helps manage server-state fetching, caching, synchronization, and mutations

questions.explanation: TanStack Query provides tools for fetching and managing asynchronous server state, including caching and refetching.

questions.text: A shopping cart must be accessed by many unrelated components. What approach might be appropriate?

options.text: Duplicate the cart in every component

questions.explanation: Shared state allows multiple parts of an application to access and update the same data consistently.

questions.text: A React application displays stale course data after an update. What could help ensure the UI reflects the latest server data?
questions.explanation: Server-state libraries can invalidate cached data and refetch updated information when mutations occur.

questions.text: What is responsive design?

options.text: Designing interfaces that adapt to different screen sizes and devices

questions.explanation: Responsive design allows interfaces to work effectively across different screen sizes and orientations.

questions.text: Which CSS technology is commonly used for two-dimensional page layouts?
questions.explanation: CSS Grid provides a powerful system for creating two-dimensional layouts.

questions.text: Which CSS technology is particularly useful for arranging items along a single row or column?
questions.explanation: Flexbox is designed for arranging elements along one-dimensional rows or columns.

questions.text: What is a reusable UI component?

options.text: A UI element designed to be used in multiple places

questions.explanation: Reusable components reduce duplication and create consistent interfaces.

sections.title: Introduction and context
sections.body: A release is ready when its important behavior is repeatable in a production build. Tests should follow what a student can observe rather than copying a component implementation.

sections.title: Lesson plan · 180 minutes
sections.body: 15 min: recall and goals; 45 min: guided explanation; 30 min: code demonstration; 10 min: break; 45 min: practical exercise; 20 min: review and quiz; 15 min: assignment briefing.

sections.title: Concepts and explanations
sections.body: Test a pure filtering function with empty and mixed input, then test the user journey of selecting a course and submitting a form. Use an integration test for the API boundary. Inspect the built bundle before optimizing; route-level lazy loading can postpone screens that the visitor has not opened. Environment variables embedded in browser bundles are public. Verify production API configuration, direct route loading and error states in a preview deployment before making the site public.

sections.title: Worked demonstration
sections.body:
Read the example, predict its output or behavior, then run it in the appropriate project. Framework snippets assume the lesson project and the shown imports or surrounding setup. Inspect the result before making the extension below.

function visibleCourses(courses, level) {
  return level === 'All' ? courses : courses.filter(c => c.level === level);
}
console.assert(visibleCourses([], 'Beginner').length === 0);

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of testing a React application?

options.text: Verify that components and application behavior work as expected

questions.explanation: Testing helps detect defects and verify expected behavior.

questions.text: What is a unit test?

options.text: A test of a small, isolated piece of functionality
A test of an entire production server

questions.explanation: Unit tests focus on small units such as functions or individual pieces of application logic.

questions.text: What is component testing commonly used to verify?
questions.explanation: Component tests can verify how components render and respond to user interactions or supplied data.

questions.text: What can unnecessary React re-renders cause?
questions.explanation: Excessive rendering can consume unnecessary CPU resources and make interfaces feel slow.

questions.text: A page renders thousands of records simultaneously and becomes slow. Which approach could improve the experience?
questions.explanation: Pagination or virtualization reduces the amount of content rendered at once.

questions.text: A React component performs an expensive calculation on every render even though its inputs rarely change. What could be considered?
questions.explanation: Memoization can avoid repeating expensive calculations when their inputs have not changed.

questions.text: What is a production build?

options.text: A Git branch that cannot be changed
An optimized version of an application intended for deployment

questions.explanation: Production builds are optimized and prepared to run in a deployment environment.

questions.text: What is the purpose of environment variables in a React application?
questions.explanation: Environment variables can provide configuration such as API base URLs and other non-secret environment-specific values.

questions.text: Which information should generally NOT be treated as a secret in a browser-based frontend?

options.text: A value that is intentionally bundled into the client application

questions.explanation: Anything shipped to a browser can potentially be inspected by users. True secrets such as database credentials and private API keys must remain on the server.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a CDN when deploying a frontend application?

options.text: Deliver static assets efficiently from geographically distributed locations

questions.explanation: A CDN caches and serves static assets such as JavaScript, CSS, images, and fonts from locations closer to users.
